html:
The law code of the Serbian Empire, adopted in 1349 at a state council under Stefan Dušan and enlarged in 1354.

Dušan had made Serbia the strongest state in the Balkans by taking large parts of Macedonia, Albania and northern Greece from the Byzantine Empire. In 1346 he was crowned emperor of the Serbs and Greeks. A new empire needed one law for its lords, churchmen and peasants.

The code mixed Serbian custom with Byzantine law, which it took from Greek legal collections translated into Slavonic. It set out the rights of the nobles and the church, the duties of dependent peasants, punishments for crimes, and rules for courts and trade.

The empire broke apart soon after Dušan died in 1355, and the Ottomans conquered the region over the next century. The code stayed in use in Serbian lands and survives in many manuscript copies. It is the best source for how medieval Serbian society worked.
sum: The law code of the Serbian Empire, adopted in 1349 at a state council under Stefan Dušan and enlarged in 1354.
